units.title: Politeness
units.intro: Grammar: reported (indirect) speech for statements, questions, requests and commands, and punctuation marks (colon, semi-colon, brackets, hyphen, apostrophe, quotation marks).

cards.title: Reported speech
rule: When the reporting verb is past (*said, asked, told*), the tense usually moves **one step back**: am/is → was; present simple → past simple; past simple → past perfect; will → would; can → could.
Pronouns and time words change: *now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, here → there*.
**Questions:** *asked + if/whether* (yes/no) or *asked + wh-word*, with **statement word order** and no question mark. **Requests/commands:** *asked/told + object + (not) to + verb*.

examples.text: She said that she was tired.
He asked me where did I live.
examples.fix: He asked me where I lived.

cards.title: When the tense does NOT change
body: 1. The reporting verb is in the **present** (*says, has said, will say*): *"I am hungry."* → *She **says** she **is** hungry.*
2. The words are a **general truth** or still true: *"Water boils at 100 °C."* → *The teacher said water **boils** at 100 °C.*
3. The verb is already **past perfect**, or a modal like **would, could, should, might, ought to**.
**say or tell?** *say* has no person after it (*She said that…*, *She said to me…*). *tell* always has a person (*She **told me** that…*). ✗ *She said me*. ✗ *She told that*.

cards.title: Step by step: report a statement
cards.problem: Report: Hana said to me, "I am going to visit my aunt in Keren tomorrow."

steps.text: **Step 1: Reporting verb.** *said to me* → **told me** (tell + person).
**Step 3: Tense one step back.** *am going to* → **was going to**.
**Step 4: Time and place words.** *tomorrow* → **the next day**. (*Keren* is a name – no change.)
**Step 5: Put it together.** Hana told me (that) she was going to visit her aunt in Keren the next day.

cards.answer: Hana told me (that) she was going to visit her aunt in Keren the next day.

cards.title: Step by step: report a question
cards.problem: Report: He asked me, "Where did you buy this book yesterday?"

steps.text: **Step 2: Statement order, no did.** *did you buy* → *you bought*.
**Step 4: Tense back.** past simple *bought* → past perfect **had bought**.
**Step 6: Full stop, not a question mark.** He asked me where I had bought that book the day before.

cards.answer: He asked me where I had bought that book the day before.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Selam said, "I have finished my homework." → Selam said that she ____ her homework.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *said* is past, so move the tense one step back.

**Step 2:** present perfect (*have finished*) → past perfect (**had finished**).

**Step 3:** *my* → *her* is already done in the sentence.

**Tip:** Change in this order: (1) reporting verb, (2) pronouns, (3) tense one step back, (4) time and place words, (5) word order for questions.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The teacher said to us, "Don't open your books." → The teacher told us ____ our books.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** It is a negative command.

**Step 2:** Pattern: told + person + **not to** + verb.

**Step 3:** So: *The teacher told us not to open our books.*

**Tip:** Change in this order: (1) reporting verb, (2) pronouns, (3) tense one step back, (4) time and place words, (5) word order for questions.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: He asked me, "Can you help me tomorrow?" → He asked me ____.

options.A: if I could help him the next day
options.C: if could I help him the next day
options.D: that I could help him tomorrow

cards.why:
**Step 1:** Yes/no question → **if / whether**.

**Step 2:** Statement order: *I could* (can → could).

**Step 3:** Pronouns: you → I, me → him. Time: tomorrow → the next day.

**Tip:** Change in this order: (1) reporting verb, (2) pronouns, (3) tense one step back, (4) time and place words, (5) word order for questions.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "I will call you tonight," Dawit said to Ruth. → Dawit told Ruth that he ____ her that night.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *will* moves back to **would**.

**Step 2:** *you* (Ruth) → *her*; *tonight* → *that night* (already in the sentence).

**Step 3:** So: *Dawit told Ruth that he would call her that night.*

**Tip:** Change in this order: (1) reporting verb, (2) pronouns, (3) tense one step back, (4) time and place words, (5) word order for questions.

cards.title: Punctuation (2)
rule: **Quotation marks** enclose the exact words in direct speech: *“I’m sorry,” she said.* **Apostrophe** shows possession (*Meron’s bag*) or a missing letter (*don’t*). **Colon (:)** introduces a list or explanation. **Semi-colon (;)** joins two closely related sentences. **Hyphen (-)** joins compound words (*well-known*). **Brackets ( )** add extra information.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "The boys bags are here."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** For a plural noun ending in -s, put the apostrophe **after** the s: *the boys' bags* (the bags of the boys). For one boy: *the boy's bag*.
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "The boys bags are here." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "The boys’ bags are here."

cards.title: Unit summary
body: In reported speech the tense moves back after a past reporting verb, pronouns and time words change, questions use if/whether or a wh-word with statement order, and requests or commands use asked/told + object + (not) to + verb.

cards.title: Step by step: Punctuation (2) – direct and reported speech
body: **Step 1:** Direct speech copies the exact words inside quotation marks: Selam said, "I am tired."
**Step 2:** Put a comma (or ? or !) before the closing quotation mark, and start the spoken words with a capital letter.
**Step 3:** Start a new line (paragraph) each time a new person speaks.
**Step 4:** Reported speech has no quotation marks: Selam said (that) she was tired – the tense moves one step back after a past reporting verb.
**Step 5:** A reported question is a statement, so it ends with a full stop, not a question mark: He asked me where I lived.
**Example:** Direct: "Where is the library?" asked Yonas. → Reported: Yonas asked where the library was. (no quotation marks, statement word order, full stop).

cards.title: Mnemonic — "Quotes for exact words, no quotes for reported words"
body: and the punctuation mark goes INSIDE the closing quotes.

cards.title: Exam tip
body: The most common error is a question mark at the end of a reported question ("He asked what my name was?"). Remove it and use statement order.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which sentence is **correctly** capitalized and punctuated?

options.A: The secretary told me “the windows are not locked.”
options.B: The director told the students, “The exam starts at 08:30am.”
options.C: She said “The electric bill reading is 62:80 nakfa.”
options.D: The invigilator asked, “Do you all have admission cards?”

cards.why: Option D follows all rules: a comma after the reporting verb, opening quotation marks, a capital letter for the start of the quote, and a question mark inside the quotation marks.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following sentences is **correctly capitalized and punctuated**?

options.A: The policeman asked," Where do you come from,"
options.B: He shouted," didn't you hear the bell?"
options.C: Tom said, "i woke up feeling ill, so I didn't go to work."
options.D: She suggested, "why don't we go out for a meal tonight?

cards.why:
**Step 1:** In direct speech, there must be a comma after 'said'.
**Step 2:** The first letter inside the quotation marks must be a **Capital Letter**.
**Step 3:** The punctuation (period, question mark) must be **inside** the quotation marks. 
Choice E follows all rules: Tom said (comma), "I'm (Capital I) feeling ill." (Period inside).

questions.tip: Change in this order: (1) reporting verb, (2) pronouns, (3) tense one step back, (4) time and place words, (5) word order for questions.

questions.q: The teacher said, "The earth goes round the sun." → The teacher said that the earth ____ round the sun.

similar.q: Report: "Water boils at 100 °C," he said.

why: A general truth does not need to change tense: **goes**.

why: Negative command: told + person + **not to** + verb.
